title: Word Search II
description:
Given an `m x n` grid of characters `board` and an array of unique strings `words`, return all words from `words` that can be constructed from letters of sequentially adjacent cells on the board.

Adjacent cells are horizontally or vertically neighboring. The same cell may not be used more than once in a single word. You may return the found words in any order, without duplicates.
constraints: board[i][j] is a lowercase English letter.
words[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
All strings in words are unique.
hints: Searching each word independently repeats huge amounts of backtracking work. Insert all candidate words into a trie first.
Run DFS from every cell on the board, advancing through the board and the trie simultaneously so branches that match no prefix are pruned immediately.

Mark cells temporarily as visited during DFS and restore them on backtrack. Clear a trie node's stored word once found (and optionally prune empty leaf nodes) to avoid duplicate results and speed up later searches.

examples.explanation: Both "oath" ((0,0) -> (0,1) -> (1,1) -> (2,1)) and "eat" ((1,3) -> (1,2) -> (1,1)) exist on the board, while "pea" and "rain" do not.
No valid horizontally or vertically adjacent path spells "abcb" without reusing cells.
